title: Acute coronary syndrome pathway
content: Suspected myocardial infarction with ST elevation requires immediate reperfusion, aspirin loading and primary percutaneous coronary intervention within 90 minutes of first medical contact. Obtain a 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes and serial troponin.

title: Type 2 diabetes treatment algorithm
content: Start lifestyle measures and metformin as first-line therapy. Add an SGLT2 inhibitor or GLP-1 receptor agonist when cardiovascular or renal disease is present. Review glycaemic control every three months.

title: Hypertension in chronic kidney disease
content: Target blood pressure below 130/80 mmHg. Prefer an ACE inhibitor or ARB when albuminuria is present and recheck creatinine and potassium within two weeks of initiation.

title: Atrial fibrillation management
content: Stratify stroke risk with CHA2DS2-VASc and start oral anticoagulation for a score of 2 or more in men and 3 or more in women. Choose rate control or rhythm control by symptoms and patient preference.

title: Sepsis recognition and first hour care
content: Screen with qSOFA or NEWS2. Give broad-spectrum antibiotics within one hour, take blood cultures first, measure lactate and give 30 mL/kg crystalloid for hypotension or lactate above 4 mmol/L.

title: Diabetic ketoacidosis protocol
content: Begin isotonic fluid resuscitation, then fixed-rate intravenous insulin. Replace potassium when serum potassium is below 5.3 mmol/L and hold insulin if potassium is below 3.3 mmol/L. Monitor glucose and ketones hourly.

title: Asthma stepwise management
content: Use an inhaled corticosteroid with formoterol as the preferred reliever and maintenance approach. Step up when symptoms occur more than twice a week and review inhaler technique before escalating.

title: Hypothyroidism diagnosis and treatment
content: Confirm persistently raised thyroid stimulating hormone with a low free thyroxine. Start levothyroxine and recheck thyroid function after six to eight weeks before adjusting the dose.

title: Chest pain with shortness of breath assessment
content: Breathlessness with pleuritic pain should prompt assessment for pulmonary embolism using the Wells score and D-dimer, and for pneumothorax and pneumonia. Image early when the pretest probability is high.

title: Stroke thrombolysis eligibility
content: Offer intravenous alteplase within 4.5 hours of symptom onset after CT excludes haemorrhage. Check glucose, blood pressure below 185/110 mmHg and anticoagulant exposure before treatment.
